newsitem.title: USA: FIELDCREST CANNON WORKERS VOTE ON UNION.
newsitem.headline: FIELDCREST CANNON WORKERS VOTE ON UNION.

text.p: Some 5,500 non-union workers at 14 Fieldcrest Cannon Inc plants in North Carolina began voting Tuesday on joining the Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees (UNITE).

Voting in what is the fourth election since 1974 seeking to unionize the Fieldcrest operations in Rowan and Cabarrus counties was scheduled to continue through late Wednesday, U.S. officials said. Results were not expected until Thursday.

A union poll, reported by The Charlotte Observer newspaper, showed that 56.8 percent of workers contacted by telephone favored joining the union while 41.5 percent did not. A UNITE spokesman was not immediately available.

The election is a court-ordered rerun of a 1991 contest won narrowly by Fieldcrest. UNITE, successor to the Amalgamated Clothing and Textile Workers Union and the International Ladies Garment Workers Union, accused Fieldcrest of harassing and firing pro-union workers in that election.

UNITE already represents about 2,500 of Fieldcrest Cannon's 10,800 U.S. manufacturing workers. The company is the largest U.S. maker of bath products and the third-largest U.S. producer of bedding products, according to Standard & Poor's Corp.
